recovery.note: This is the analyser-independent ground truth and the reason the pair is tier A and recall-eligible: the fix in 1.8.5's ECDSA signing removes the exploitable nonce-bit-length leak, so the same lattice attack that recovers the 1.8.4 key fails on 1.8.5.

primitive_timing.probe: acquire/ecmul_timing_probe.c, rdtscp minimum rdtscp ticks (the key name says cycles; the probe reads rdtscp, corrected 2026-09-02) for gcry_mpi_ec_mul over a short vs a full secure-memory scalar, one core
primitive_timing.interpretation: The public scalar-multiplication primitive's time depends on the scalar bit-length in BOTH versions (the short scalar is multiplied in roughly half the cycles): it is unchanged across the patch. 1.8.5's fix lives in the internal ECDSA signing path, where the nonce is a secure-memory MPI whose scalar multiplication is clamped to the field bit-length, which the public gcry_mpi_ec_mul does not reach. A timing test pointed at the primitive therefore cannot discriminate the two builds; the end-to-end recovery, which exercises real signing, is what discriminates them. This is why the pair is scored by recovery, not by a per-arm analyser verdict, and it is recorded rather than turned into a tool row that would report a property of the public API rather than of the deployed fix.
